answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The summit multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and pigment lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 2807 identities would post 944 proofs and burn roughly 65 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
